quarterly_data.signal: Vertical integration DOWN into owned data centers is now visible: 'you are starting to see the first 2 to 3 of our self-builds spin up', with more to come. CEO says the margin recapture is the lesser reason — the bigger one is control and a 'better sandbox' to run the flywheel of data-center innovations it then applies across its fleet. Management expects continued effort to control the physical infrastructure both up and down the stack.
quarterly_data.figure: first 2 to 3 of our self-builds spinning up

quarterly_data.signal: NVIDIA has designated CoreWeave's software stack as a REFERENCE ARCHITECTURE, and CoreWeave is now selling that stack — branded 'Omni' — to third parties to run on THEIR infrastructure. Management frames it as leverage on other balance sheets: it can serve customers that want to own their own infrastructure, and reach jurisdictions where CoreWeave is not comfortable owning an asset-heavy position, expanding TAM without capex. One such deal closed 'a couple of months ago' with 'a whole bunch coming down the pipe'.

Software attach metric repeated and put in context: '75% of our clients are using three different services' — three separate silos of the product suite already being consumed — and management argues the true rate is higher because some clients are early-stage ventures not yet on product two or three. The roadmap (storage, memory, networking, managed inference, international low-latency capacity) is client-led.
quarterly_data.figure: 75% of our clients are using three different services

quarterly_data.signal: Capital-structure detail beyond the call: the largest engine of borrowing is at the SPV level, where lenders underwrite by looking through to the credit of the offtake ('it's Microsoft on the other side of this transaction'), with cash flowing into the SPV to repay the debt before it reaches CoreWeave; debt also sits at the parent plus convertibles. Two firsts cited: the most recent structure is the first time lenders have been willing to take RENEWAL RISK (which unlocks financing against short-term contracts), and an earlier venture-rated deal let CoreWeave borrow at A- credit, which management says puts its borrowing at or close to par with hyperscalers.
quarterly_data.figure: borrowing at A- credit; first debt structure where lenders take renewal risk
